title: American Fusion Expands Patent Portfolio to 130 Applications as National Exchange Uplisting Plans Advance
excerpt: The fusion technology developer has reached halfway toward its year-end patent filing target while evaluating TXSE and Nasdaq listing pathways and potential...
content_html:
Fiona Craig

Tue, September 8, 2026 at 10:04 AM CDT 3 min read

The fusion technology developer has reached halfway toward its year-end patent filing target while evaluating TXSE and Nasdaq listing pathways and potential financing options.

Key Investor Takeaways

  • American Fusion (USOTC:AMFN) filed 30 additional U.S. patent applications, expanding its Texatron Fusion Engine intellectual property portfolio to 130 pending applications.

  • The American Fusion patent portfolio has now reached approximately half of the company's stated goal of more than 260 U.S. applications by the end of 2026.

  • The company is evaluating a potential national exchange uplisting from OTCQB, with both the Texas Stock Exchange and Nasdaq under consideration and TXSE currently the preferred potential venue.

  • American Fusion has received several financing term sheets that could support an uplisting and provide capital for Texatron commercialization, but no definitive financing agreement has been signed.

  • Both major developments remain subject to execution risk: patent applications must undergo USPTO examination, while any uplisting requires the company to satisfy applicable exchange standards and receive approval.

Why AMFN Stock Is in Focus

American Fusion has expanded its pending U.S. patent portfolio by 30 applications to 130 as it simultaneously advances preparations for a potential move to a national securities exchange.

The latest filings broaden intellectual property coverage around the company's proprietary Texatron Fusion Engine. They address configurations and components including aluminum fusion-confinement structures, toroidal and rifled chamber designs, conductive components, helium-3 and deuterium fuel-injection systems and electronic pulse controls.

The filing pace has accelerated since American Fusion announced 100 pending U.S. patent applications on August 24. The company ultimately aims to exceed 260 applications by year-end.

Importantly, these remain patent applications rather than granted patents. Each is subject to examination by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, with no assurance that individual applications will result in issued patents.

Why This Matters for Investors

The expanding patent portfolio could strengthen American Fusion's efforts to protect different configurations of the Texatron platform as engineering and validation continue. Reaching 130 applications also provides a measurable indicator of progress against the company's stated 2026 intellectual property target.

At the same time, the capital-markets initiative could become increasingly relevant to the company's commercialization strategy.
